full_judgment:
2. The petitioner Muktad Hossain Majumder filed Election Tribunal Case No. 4 of 1984 before the Upazila Munsif, Chauddagram and Election Tribunal for a declaration that the election of Chairman of No. 5 Suvapur Union Parishad held on 27-2-83 is void and for an order that fresh polls be held with regard to Kadghar Primary School Centre. The Election Tribunal after taking evidence in the matter set aside the election of that centre and ordered for fresh poll's, by its judgment and order dated 19-11-84 against which the elected Chairman i.e. the opposite party Abul Bashar Majumder preferred Election Tribunal Appeal No. 14 of 1984 before the learned District Judge, Camilla. The appeal was fixed for hearing on 7-5-85. 

 3. The petitioner, being respondent in the appeal, was present in the Court, but the opposite party, being the appellant, was not present. The learned District Judge, Comilla dismissed the appeal for default by his judgment and order dated 7-5-85. The opposite party thereafter filed an application under Order XLI, rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure, being Miscellaneous Case No. 109 of 1985 for restoration of the Election Appeal. The petitioner objected to the restoration and after hearing both the parties the learned District Judge, Comilla by his order dated 30-5-85 allowed the application for the opposite party under Order XLI, rule 19 CPC and fixed a date for hearing of the election appeal. 

 4. Mr. Md Amir Hossain, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits only one point, namely, that the learned District Judge as the appellate forum of an election petition has no jurisdiction to entertain an application under Order XLI, rule 19, CPC. His submission is that the Election Tribunal itself is not a Civil Court within the meaning of section 3 of the Civil Courts Act 1887. Under Rule 48 of the Union Parishads (Election) Rules, 1983 the Election Tribunal shall have all the powers of a Civil Court trying a suit under the Code of Civil Procedure and shall be deemed to be a Civil Court within the meaning of sections 481 and 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, but the Tribunal does not become a Civil Court thereby Such a Tribunal cannot exercise jurisdiction under Order 9, rule 13 CPC or under Order 39, rules 1 and 2 CPC When it allows or dismisses an Election Case, either exparte or by default or on contest, it becomes functus officio and thereafter it has no jurisdiction to entertain and continue a fresh proceedings under Order 9, rule 13 CPC Mr Amir Hossain submits that this is the view which has been consistently taken in respect of Tribunals set up under Special Statutes, e.g. in the case of Khulna Tobacco Industries Ltd. vs Chairman, Labour Court, Khulna and another 30 DLR 331, Mohammad Sharijullah vs Election Tribunal, 31 DLR 119. 

 5. Mr Md. Amir Hussain submits that the powers and functions of the appellate forum that decides appeals from election disputes cannot be higher than the powers and functions of the Tribunal trying the dispute as a trial Court. As the Election Tribunal itself cannot entertain an application under Order 9 rule 13 CPC, the appellate forum also cannot entertain on application under Order XLI, rule 19 CPC. He submits that the learned District Judge becomes functus officio after he allows or dismisses an election appeal, either exparte or by default or on contest. Under Order XLI, Yule 19 CPC the lies between the parties is whether the applicant was prevented by any sufficient cause from being present in Court when the appeal was called on for hearing. A separate miscellaneous case is usually started on that application and it is a completely new matter which the appellate Court is called upon to decide. Mr. Amir Hossain submits that under the amended section 29 (4) of the Local Government Ordinance, 1984 the learned District Judge is required to adjudicate on the decision of the Election Tribunal. He is not to adjudicate on any other matter. 

 9. Following a long line of decisions on the point as to what is the true meaning and import of the expression "District Judge" in the aforesaid statute, I have no hesitation in holding that the expression "District Judge" occurring in section 29(4) of the Local Government Ordinance, 1984 means a Court and not a persona designata. Reference may be made of the case of Amir Sultan Ali Haider vs Mohammad K. Ali, 29 DLR (SC) 295. The District Judge is not only a Court but under section 3(17) of the General Clauses Act, 1897 the said expression means Judge of a principal Civil Court of original Civil Jurisdiction. It is a Civil Court within the meaning of section 3 of the Civil Courts Act, 1887. 

 In spite of the incongruity of a revisional application being available to a party aggrieved against the substantive decision of the District Judge on the Election Appeal and of there being a provision for appeal in the case of a rejection of an application under Order XLI, rule 19 CPC, the District Judge will continue to exercise all those powers which as an appellate Court has been vested in him under the Code of Civil Procedure. The lawmaker fully understood the implication of bestowing the appellate power to the principal Civil Court of original jurisdiction and was therefore mindful of the consequences of doing so.
